toolset-must-match-vcpkg: The x64-*-aec3 presets link a PREBUILT static WebRTC, and a prebuilt
library constrains the TOOLSET the same way it constrains the CRT.
MSVC's separately-compiled STL grows new entry points over time --
__std_find_first_of_trivial_pos_1, __std_min_element_f,
__std_max_element_f, __std_minmax_element_f -- so objects compiled by a
NEWER toolset call into things an OLDER libcpmt.lib has never defined.
The failure is LNK2001 on symbols nobody in this repo wrote, at the end
of a very long link.
THE TRAP: vcpkg picks the NEWEST Visual Studio instance on the box, and
this repo does not -- it pins "Visual Studio 17 2022". Install VS 18
alongside VS 2022 and the two silently diverge (vcpkg -> 14.50 / v145,
repo -> v143). Nothing warns; the packages build 18/18 clean and the
mismatch only surfaces at link time.
THE FIX, and it is committed: cmake/vcpkg-triplets/x64-windows-static.cmake
is an overlay triplet that pins VCPKG_VISUAL_STUDIO_PATH to the VS 2022
install. Install WebRTC through it -- see cmake/WebRtcAec3.cmake for the
command -- so the dependency follows the project rather than the box.
SECOND, SMALLER TRAP, on the repo side. Within one VS 2022 install these
two files can still disagree:
VC/Auxiliary/Build/Microsoft.VCToolsVersion.default.txt       <- vcvars64, hence vcpkg
VC/Auxiliary/Build/Microsoft.VCToolsVersion.v143.default.txt  <- MSBuild, hence this repo
If they do, pin the version vcpkg used (the FIRST file) on both the
configure AND the build preset:
"environment": { "VCToolsVersion": "<x.y.z>" }
NOT "toolset": {"value": "version=<x.y.z>"} -- that is the field which
looks correct and does not work. CMake accepts it and sets
CMAKE_GENERATOR_TOOLSET, but emits no <VCToolsVersion> into the
generated .vcxproj, so MSBuild resolves v143 through the file above and
compiles with the old toolset anyway. Measured, not assumed. The env var
works because v143.default.props assigns its value under
Condition="'$(VCToolsVersion)' == ''", which an env var satisfies.
It must be on the BUILD preset too: build presets do not inherit the
configure preset's environment, and the build is where it matters.
That version is a property of the machine, not of the project, so it
belongs in CMakeUserPresets.json -- exactly like VCPKG_ROOT.
Changing the toolset invalidates the cache in an existing tree: CMake
refuses to reconfigure when the compiler moves. Delete CMakeCache.txt
and CMakeFiles/ and reconfigure -- do NOT delete the whole tree. _deps/
is over 2 GB of fetched ONNXRuntime, DirectStorage and WebView2, it
survives a cache wipe, and a fresh binaryDir re-downloads all of it.
Then build with --clean-first: deleting the cache does NOT invalidate
the per-project .obj files, so an ordinary rebuild relinks stale objects
from the previous toolset and quietly defeats the whole exercise.

configurePresets.name: aec3
configurePresets.description: Resolves the prebuilt WebRTC package so cmake/WebRtcAec3.cmake finds it. The STATIC triplet is mandatory -- the root pins a static CRT (CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY), and x64-windows builds against the dynamic one; mixing them is LNK2038 at the very end of a very long link. Both triplet roots are listed so this composes with the cloud leg, which resolves libcurl/simdjson from x64-windows. THE TOOLSET MUST ALSO MATCH, and this preset cannot pin it portably -- see the toolset-must-match note in the vendor block below.

configurePresets.name: x64-release-aec3
configurePresets.description: The configuration the live echo-cancellation work is measured in. RELEASE ON PURPOSE: the Debug webrtc.lib is ~650 MB against ~73 MB for Release, and AEC3's filter bank is not something to run unoptimised on the capture thread.
